title_en: Liyuan Company v. Jinlanwan Company — dispute over trademark infringement
ruling_gist_en: Where a seller of commercial housing, in its advertising, uses a place name contained in another person's registered trademark to indicate the geographical location of the commercial housing, and such use does not cause the public to be confused or mistaken as to the source of the commercial housing, it does not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark.
keywords_en: civil; trademark infringement dispute; second instance; Higher People's Court; Jiangsu Province; legal person; Trademark Law; General Principles of Civil Law; fair use of geographic trademarks; trademark infringement determination; likelihood of confusion; affirm the original judgment; trademark registration; real estate advertisement; use of place name; good faith; dispute over trademark infringement against Jinlan Bay Company
full_text_en:
Liyuan Company v. Jinlanwan Company — dispute over trademark infringement

【Ruling Summary】

Where a commercial housing sales entity uses a place name contained in another person's registered trademark to indicate the geographical location of the commercial housing in its advertising and publicity, and such use does not cause confusion or misidentification among the public as to the source of the commercial housing, it does not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

Plaintiff: Nanjing Liyuan Property Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Yan Lugen, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Defendant: Nanjing Jinlanwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Changfu Street, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Jin Xihe, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The plaintiff, Nanjing Liyuan Property Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Liyuan Company), filed a lawsuit against the defendant, Nanjing Jinlanwan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinlanwan Company), for trademark infringement. The case was accepted by the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff alleged: After nine years of investment amounting to hundreds of millions of yuan, the plaintiff developed the Baijia Lake Garden and meticulously built the Baijia Lake Garden into a well-known brand in the real estate industry, which has enormous economic value. In 2000, the plaintiff obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Baijia Lake". On October 10, 2001, without the plaintiff's permission, the defendant named its newly developed high-rise residential building 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 and used this name for advertising. The use of the characters "Baijia Lake" in this name infringed upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. The plaintiff requested a judgment ordering the defendant to immediately cease the infringement, publicly apologize, compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 1,000,000, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff submitted the following evidence:

1. Trademark registration certificate, to prove that Liyuan Company is the owner of the exclusive right to use the cursive script character trademark "Baijia Lake";
2. Advertising expenses and advertising samples for "Baijia Lake Garden®", and a newspaper real estate advertising monitoring report, to prove Liyuan Company's investment in promoting the registered trademark;
3. A sales brochure of Jinlanwan Company, the *Jinling Evening News* on October 10, 12, and 17, 2001, the *Yangtze Evening Post* on November 11, 2001, and four photos of the model houses exhibited by Jinlanwan Company at the Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, to prove the infringement by Jinlanwan Company;
4. Price list for "Fengqing States", to prove the potential benefits Jinlanwan Company may have gained from the infringement.

The defendant argued: The "Fengqing States" high-rise residential building developed and constructed by the defendant is located in the Baijia Lake area of Jiangning District, Nanjing. The defendant's use of "Baijia Lake" before the name of the building constitutes use of a place name. The defendant's naming of the building only requires approval from the Place Names Committee of Jiangning District, Nanjing, and does not require a trademark license from the plaintiff. "Baijia Lake" is a well-known place name. The defendant's use of 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 in its advertising was to let consumers understand the location of the "Fengqing States" high-rise residential building, not to cause consumers to mistake the "Fengqing States" high-rise residential building developed by the defendant for the plaintiff's property. The plaintiff's claims are groundless and should be dismissed.

The defendant submitted the following evidence:

1. *Jiangning County Place Name Directory of Jiangsu Province*, Jiangning County place name map, and the approval document of the Place Names Committee of Jiangning District, Nanjing, regarding the naming of "Fengqing Homeland", to prove that "Baijia Lake" is a place name, and "Fengqing States" is a high-rise residential building developed within "Fengqing Homeland";
2. An explanation from Jiangsu Genesis Communication Co., Ltd. regarding the mark 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】, to prove that the mark was only used to indicate the location of the "Fengqing States" high-rise residential building.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

Baijia Lake is a place name within Dongshan Town, Jiangning District, Nanjing. On October 14, 2000, upon approval by the State Trademark Office, the plaintiff Liyuan Company obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Baijia Lake". The trademark mark is the cursive script of the characters "Baijia Lake", registered in Class 36 of services, and the approved scope of services is: appraisal of works of art, real estate rental, real estate agency, real estate brokerage, real estate appraisal, real estate management, apartment management, apartment rental, residence (apartments), and brokerage. In September and October 2001, Liyuan Company published various property sale advertisements in *Modern Express* using the form "Baijia Lake Garden®" in cursive script.

On September 14, 2001, upon approval by the Place Names Committee of Jiangning District, the residential community developed by the defendant Jinlanwan Company in the Baijia Lake area of Jiangning District was named "Fengqing Homeland". Jinlanwan Company named its newly launched high-rise residential building within "Fengqing Homeland" as 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 and used this name to publish property sale advertisements in the *Jinling Evening News* on October 10, 12, and 17, 2001, and in the *Yangtze Evening Post* on November 11, 2001. In Jinlanwan Company's sales brochure, there was the text mark 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】, and at the lower right of the mark pattern, there was also the text "Baijia Lake · Fengqing States". On the model houses exhibited at the Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, Jinlanwan Company used the advertising slogan 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held:

Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law) provides: "In civil activities, the principles of voluntariness, fairness, making compensation for equal value, and good faith shall be observed." Article 5 provides: "The lawful civil rights and interests of citizens and legal persons shall be protected by law; no organization or individual may infringe upon them." Article 51 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law) provides: "The exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be limited to the trademark approved for registration and the goods approved for use." Article 52, paragraph 1, item (1) provides that using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on identical or similar goods without the permission of the trademark registrant constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark.

To determine trademark infringement, it must first be determined whether the allegedly infringing text, graphics, etc., are identical or similar to the text, graphics, etc., of the registered trademark, and second, whether the allegedly infringing goods or services are identical or similar to the goods or services approved for use with the registered trademark, and whether they could cause confusion among consumers as to the source of the goods or services. Since the plaintiff Liyuan Company's registered trademark contains the place name "Baijia Lake", in determining whether the defendant Jinlanwan Company's conduct constitutes infringement, it must also be determined whether Jinlanwan Company's use of the place name was in good faith and reasonable.

The plaintiff Liyuan Company registered the cursive script character trademark "Baijia Lake", and the exclusive right to use this registered trademark should be protected by law. The company actually used its trademark in the form of "Baijia Lake Garden®". Although this form of use does not comply with legal requirements, it does not affect the company's exclusive right to use the "Baijia Lake" registered trademark. The defendant Jinlanwan Company named its developed property 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 and also used the same text in its advertising. Although Jinlanwan Company used "Baijia Lake" in printed form different from the cursive script, it still contained these three characters.

The approved scope of use for the registered trademark "Baijia Lake" includes real estate services, but does not include real estate development and construction. The defendant Jinlanwan Company naming its self-developed high-rise building 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 does not conflict with the approved scope of use of the "Baijia Lake" registered trademark. However, the act of selling houses by Jinlanwan Company after completing the real estate development is similar to the approved scope of use of the "Baijia Lake" registered trademark.

The Trademark Law does not prohibit the registration of place names below the level of county-level administrative divisions as trademarks. Place names are part of the public domain vocabulary, and the public's legitimate and reasonable use of place names cannot be excluded. Where a place name is registered as a trademark, the trademark right should be subject to certain limitations. A distinctive feature of real estate sales is that they must be linked to the corresponding geographical location. Only by informing buyers of the geographical location of the real estate can a seller attract purchases. The 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 high-rise residential building developed by the defendant Jinlanwan Company is located in the Baijia Lake area of Jiangning District. Jinlanwan Company's use of the characters "Baijia Lake" in the advertising slogan for the sale of this high-rise residential building was intended to inform buyers of the geographical location of the property, which constitutes a reasonable use in good faith of the place name "Baijia Lake". At the same time, the plaintiff Liyuan Company actually used the "Baijia Lake" trademark in the form of "Baijia Lake Garden®", while Jinlanwan Company promoted its developed property as 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】. Generally, consumers would not mistake 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 for "Baijia Lake Garden".

In summary, the plaintiff Liyuan Company's lawsuit accusing the defendant Jinlanwan Company of infringing its exclusive right to use the registered trademark and seeking compensation of RMB 1,000,000 in economic losses lacks a sufficient legal basis and is not supported. Accordingly, on April 3, 2002, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court entered the following judgment:

The plaintiff Liyuan Company's claims are dismissed.

Case acceptance fee of RMB 15,010 shall be borne by the plaintiff Liyuan Company.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Liyuan Company refused to accept it and filed an appeal. The reasons are: 1. Ten years ago, Baijia Lake was only a small pond. Only after the Jiangning Development Zone and the appellant invested huge sums of money to meticulously build it did Baijia Lake become a scenic area with significant economic value. "Baijia Lake" is the appellant's well-known brand. The approved place name for the development area of the appellee is "Fengqing Homeland"; the "Fengqing States" property developed by the appellee is located east of Shengtai Road and west of Jing'er Road in Jiangning District, separated from Baijia Lake by Baijia Lake Garden villa clusters, World Village villa clusters, several multi-story apartment buildings, and a road; the location of "Fengqing States" cannot in any way be associated with Baijia Lake or the shores of Baijia Lake; using the three characters "Baijia Lake" to indicate the geographical location of this property is not reasonable; the appellee's unauthorized naming of this property as 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 was intended to exploit the market influence of the appellant's well-known brand to promote its own property, causing consumers to misunderstand the origin of the "Fengqing States" property. 2. The State Administration for Industry and Commerce stipulates that normal use of customary service industry marks, and normal use of trade names (firm names), names, place names, and names of service venues to indicate service characteristics or to describe service matters, etc., does not constitute infringement of service trademark exclusive rights, unless there is a clear intent of unfair competition. The appellee did not use the three characters "Baijia Lake" to describe the geographical location of the "Fengqing States" property, but used these characters as part of the property's name and text trademark. This manner of use can only cause consumers to misidentify the source of the goods or services; the appellee only obtained the *Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit* on November 5, 2001, but as early as October 2001, before obtaining the pre-sale permit, the appellee published real estate advertisements in violation of the national regulation that "no real estate advertisements may be published before obtaining the pre-sale permit", using 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 to promote its property; after the appellant filed the first-instance lawsuit, the appellee gradually changed from the initially used 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 to 【Baijia Lake Shore · Fengqing States】, or 【Fengqing States】. All this demonstrates that the appellee's use of the characters "Baijia Lake" to promote its developed property was subjectively intentional infringement, not bona fide use, and constituted unfair competition. The first-instance finding that the appellee's use of the place name was reasonable and in good faith lacks factual basis and legal support. Therefore, the appellant requests the appellate court to reverse the original judgment and uphold the claims made in the first instance.

The evidence submitted by the appellant Liyuan Company in the second instance is:

1. The sales brochure of Jinlanwan Company and a shopping bag printed with the words 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】. The sales brochure names the property as 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】, Baijia Lake Shore · Fengqing States, and 【Fengqing States】, to prove that Jinlanwan Company's use of the words 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 was intentional infringement;
2. Advertisements for properties of other real estate companies published in *Jinling Evening News*, *Yangzhou Evening News*, etc., to prove that Jinlanwan Company's description of the property's geographical location differed from the customary expressions of others in the same industry.

The appellee Jinlanwan Company argued in its defense: Baijia Lake has become a scenic area, and it represents not a single point but a region. The "Baijia Lake · Fengqing States" property is indeed located in the Baijia Lake area. The appellee's use of "Baijia Lake" in naming its property was intended to indicate the geographical location of the property, a use that complies with the regulations of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce. The appellant's grounds for appeal are untenable and should be dismissed, and the original judgment should be affirmed. The appellee Jinlanwan Company did not submit new evidence in the second instance.

The Jiangsu High People's Court found in the second instance: On the model houses exhibited at the Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, the appellee Jinlanwan Company used the advertising slogan 【Baijia Lake Shore · Fengqing States】, where the character "Shore" was noticeably smaller than the other characters. Apart from this, the second instance confirmed the other facts found in the first instance.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held in the second instance:

The alleged infringing conduct in this case occurred before the second revision of the Trademark Law came into effect. Article 41(2) of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (prior to revision) provides that using words or designs identical or similar to a registered trademark on identical or similar goods as a product name or product decoration, where it is sufficient to cause confusion, constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as referred to in Article 38(4) of the Trademark Law. The appellant Liyuan Company obtained the registered trademark "Baijia Lake" upon approval by the State Trademark Office, and this registered trademark should be protected by law. The "Baijia Lake" trademark is a Class 36 service trademark, with the scope of use being real estate services; real estate sales are similar to Class 36 services. The appellee Jinlanwan Company's use of the characters "Baijia Lake" in its advertisements and sales brochures for the sale of commercial housing does not constitute bona fide use.

First, the appellee Jinlanwan Company named its property 【Baijia Lake Shore · Fengqing States】, where the three characters "Baijia Lake" were used side by side with the property name, in a prominent position; however, in the description of the property's geographical location, it was not stated that the property was located on the shore of Baijia Lake, which could easily cause consumers to mistakenly believe that the property was associated with "Baijia Lake Garden".

Second, in the advertising slogan on the model houses exhibited at the Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, the appellee Jinlanwan Company emphasized the three characters "Baijia Lake" while downplaying the character "Shore", indicating that the company intended to attract consumers' attention to "Baijia Lake", rather than using "Baijia Lake" to indicate the geographical location of the property being sold.

Third, the appellee Jinlanwan Company's property is not located on the shore of Baijia Lake; there are several other real estate companies' properties between it and Baijia Lake. Jinlanwan Company's use of 【Baijia Lake Shore · Fengqing States】 carries a certain degree of falsity.

The appellee Jinlanwan Company's conduct has gone beyond the scope of bona fide use and infringed upon the appellant Liyuan Company's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Baijia Lake". The appellant Liyuan Company's grounds for appeal are well-founded and should be adopted.

Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction and Scope of Application of Law in Trial of Trademark Cases provides: "For cases filed after the entry into force of the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law concerning infringing acts that occurred before the entry into force of the Decision, where the people's court has not yet rendered a final judgment by the time the Decision enters into force, Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law shall be applied by reference." Article 134, items (1) and (10) of the General Principles of Civil Law provide that a person who infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of another shall bear civil liability by ceasing the infringement and making an apology. Article 56 of the revised Trademark Law provides that the amount of damages for infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be the profit gained by the infringer during the period of infringement as a result of the infringement, or the loss suffered by the infringed party during the period of infringement as a result of the infringement, including the reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed party to stop the infringement; where the profit gained by the infringer or the loss suffered by the infringed party is difficult to determine, the people's court shall, in light of the circumstances of the infringement, render a judgment for damages of not more than RMB 500,000. The appellant Liyuan Company claimed damages of RMB 1,000,000, using the appellee Jinlanwan Company's profits from infringement as the calculation standard. However, the evidence submitted by Liyuan Company does not have a necessary connection with its claims, the illegal profits of Jinlanwan Company from trademark infringement are difficult to determine, and the direct losses suffered by Liyuan Company due to the infringement are also difficult to ascertain. Therefore, the court shall determine the amount based on the actual circumstances of this case.

In summary, the first instance applied the revised Trademark Law as the basis and found that the appellee Jinlanwan Company did not constitute infringement, which was an erroneous application of law and should be reversed. Accordingly, on September 19, 2002, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, entered the following judgment:

I. The first-instance civil judgment is reversed;
II. The appellee Jinlanwan Company shall immediately cease the infringement of the appellant Liyuan Company's exclusive right to use the registered trademark;
III. The appellee Jinlanwan Company shall compensate the appellant Liyuan Company for economic losses of RMB 100,000, to be paid in a lump sum within 10 days after this judgment takes effect;
IV. The appellee Jinlanwan Company shall publish an apology in the *Jinling Evening News* within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, the content of which shall be subject to court review.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances are each RMB 15,010, with the appellant Liyuan Company bearing RMB 3,000 each, and the appellee Jinlanwan Company bearing RMB 12,010 each.

After the second-instance judgment was pronounced, Jinlanwan Company refused to accept it and applied to the Jiangsu High People's Court for retrial, arguing: 1. "Baijia Lake" was developed through the investment of the Jiangning District Government and numerous real estate developers, not solely by the respondent Liyuan Company. How could it become the respondent's exclusive well-known brand? The place name "Baijia Lake" existed before the development of the area. When "Baijia Lake" is mentioned, the general public in Nanjing first thinks of it as a place name or a lake name; few people know it is the respondent's trademark. The respondent's registration of "Baijia Lake" as a trademark was an attempt to monopolize the development achievements of the District Government and numerous real estate developers. 2. "Baijia Lake" is a well-known place name in Nanjing. It represents not a single point or a line but a region. The applicant's property is located in this region. The primary characteristic of real estate sales is the need to be linked to the corresponding geographical location. The applicant's use of 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 to name and advertise its property was a reasonable use of a geographical indication; any resident of Nanjing would understand that it means the "Fengqing States" property is located at Baijia Lake. On the model houses exhibited at the Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, due to layout constraints, the applicant made the character "Shore" in the slogan 【Baijia Lake Shore Fengqing States】 smaller. The second instance's finding that the applicant's use "was not in good faith" is unjustified. 3. The applicant's naming of its property as 【Baijia Lake · Fengqing States】 was by no means intended to cause consumers to mistake this property for the respondent's property. Moreover, the applicant's property name is neither identical nor similar to the respondent's registered trademark, and consumers would not be confused. The second-instance judgment is erroneous, and the applicant requests a retrial to amend it.

Liyuan Company argued in its defense: 1. The retrial applicant's use of the same text as the respondent's registered trademark as a prefix for a commercial housing project on identical goods constituted an infringement of the respondent's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. 2. The retrial applicant directly used "Baijia Lake" as a sign for goods, which was sufficient to cause confusion and mistaken recognition among the relevant public, i.e., ordinary homebuyers. 3. The "Baijia Lake" trademark enjoys high reputation in the Nanjing area. The retrial applicant's use of this trademark to promote commercial housing constituted clear malicious use and unfair competition. The judgment of the second instance was correct and should be affirmed.

The Jiangsu High People's Court, upon retrial, confirmed that the facts found in the original first and second instance judgments were true.

The issue in dispute in this case was whether the retrial applicant's use of the words "Baijia Lake" in its real estate project advertisements infringed upon the respondent's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Baijia Lake".

The Jiangsu High People's Court held in the retrial as follows:

"Baijia Lake" is a lawfully registered trademark with the State Trademark Office, and the respondent, Liyuan Company, enjoys an exclusive right to use this trademark. However, this trademark is a word mark containing a geographical name. While protecting the exclusive right to use the trademark in accordance with the law, legitimate public interests must also be reasonably maintained. Article 37 of the Trademark Law before its amendment provides: "The exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be limited to the trademark that has been approved for registration and the goods for which the use of the trademark has been approved." As the holder of the exclusive right to use the trademark, Liyuan Company has the right to prohibit others from using a mark that is identical or similar to the registered trademark on identical or similar goods or services, but it does not have the right to prohibit others from legitimately using the geographical name contained in the registered trademark on identical or similar goods to indicate the connection between the goods and their place of origin or geographical location.

The determination of whether trademark exclusive rights are infringed depends primarily on whether the general attention of the relevant public would cause confusion or mistaken recognition as to the source of the identical or similar goods or services. Although the retrial applicant, Jinlanwan Company, used the same words as the registered trademark in its real estate project naming and advertising, this does not constitute infringement of the respondent Liyuan Company's exclusive right to use the trademark. The reasons are as follows:

First, in the Baijia Lake area, there are names such as "Baijia Lake Subdistrict Office," "Baijia Lake Middle School," and "Baijia Lake Primary School." It is evident that "Baijia Lake" is primarily used as a place name and a lake name; "Baijia Lake" is known because of the geographical location. Although the respondent, Liyuan Company, participated in early property development and environmental improvement in the Baijia Lake area, the Baijia Lake area was developed mainly through the input of the Nanjing Jiangning District Government and numerous real estate developers around the lake, and was not developed solely by Liyuan Company. For the ordinary public in Nanjing, the first impression of "Baijia Lake" is a place name and a lake name; it is generally not regarded as a trademark. As a place name and lake name, "Baijia Lake" belongs to the vocabulary of the public domain. At least before the dispute arose, its recognition as a Class 36 trademark was low. In geographical trademarks, if the words used are known because of the trademark, the likelihood of confusion or mistaken recognition among the relevant public is high; if the words used are known because of the geographical area, the likelihood of confusion or mistaken recognition is low. The Baijia Lake trademark and the Baijia Lake place name are not easily confused.

Second, the nature of real estate sales requires a connection with the corresponding geographical location. Indicating the geographical location of a real estate project is a business practice in real estate sales determined by the characteristics of the real estate itself. The real estate project developed by the retrial applicant, Jinlanwan Company, is located in the Baijia Lake area, very close to the lake. Jinlanwan Company is fully entitled to use the words "Baijia Lake" to truthfully indicate the geographical location of the commercial housing. Jinlanwan Company named its project "[Baijia Lake·Fengqing Guodu]" and used "[Baijia Lake·Fengqing Guodu]" or "[Fengqing Guodu by Baijia Lake]" in advertisements, for the purpose of informing consumers that the project is located in the Baijia Lake area. This purpose and manner of use are consistent with the ordinary public's common understanding of indicating a project's geographical location and conform to the business practices of real estate sales. It is a legitimate use of a place name.

Third, housing is real estate, and its geographical characteristics are very pronounced. Consumers are more cautious when purchasing housing than when purchasing other goods. They often compare different projects repeatedly and, even when buying well-known brand commercial housing, typically conduct on-site inspections. They do not blindly choose solely because of brand recognition. Given the level of attention of the relevant public when selecting such goods, the use of "[Baijia Lake·Fengqing Guodu]" or "[Fengqing Guodu by Baijia Lake]" by the retrial applicant, Jinlanwan Company, in its promotions would not cause confusion or mistaken recognition among the relevant public as to the source of the commercial housing.

Fourth, "Fengqing Guodu" is the real estate project developed by the retrial applicant, Jinlanwan Company. There is no need for the company to attribute its real estate to the respondent, Liyuan Company. The manner in which Jinlanwan Company used the words "Baijia Lake" does not create a suggestion linking the "Fengqing Guodu" project to the registered trademark "Baijia Lake". Even if Jinlanwan Company removed the words "Baijia Lake" from its sales brochures and other promotional materials after Liyuan Company initiated the first instance lawsuit, this cannot lead to the conclusion that its initial use of the words "Baijia Lake" was made with malicious intent to infringe.

In summary, the use of the words "Baijia Lake" by the retrial applicant, Jinlanwan Company, in the process of selling its own real estate project would not cause confusion or mistaken recognition among the relevant public. It is fair and reasonable use. The Trademark Law was amended on October 27, 2001, and came into effect on December 1, 2001. In determining the nature of the advertising act "[Baijia Lake·Fengqing Guodu]" occurring in October 2001, the first instance court improperly applied the amended Trademark Law as the basis for judgment. However, its conclusion that Jinlanwan Company's actions did not constitute infringement was correct and should be affirmed. The second instance court found the facts clearly, but its judgment that Jinlanwan Company's fair use constituted infringement was an improper application of the law and should be corrected. Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 184, paragraph 1 and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on December 20, 2004, rendered the following judgment:

1. Set aside the civil judgment of the original second instance;
2. Affirm the civil judgment of the original first instance, i.e., dismiss the claims of the respondent, Liyuan Company.
The court acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance proceedings, each RMB 15,010, shall be borne by the respondent, Liyuan Company.
